Modified assessment with Beige Book overlay:
- FOMC (July 27, 2022) remains clearly hawkish: activity softened but job gains robust; inflation elevated; rates raised 75 bps to 2.25–2.50% with guidance for ongoing hikes and balance-sheet runoff accelerating in September.
- SLOOS corroborates tighter credit supply: banks tightened standards and terms across C&I, CRE, RRE, HELOCs, and consumer credit; pricing and collateral requirements up; reasons include weaker outlook and liquidity concerns. Demand mixed (stronger for C&I and HELOCs, weaker for CRE).
- Beige Book signals add downside risk to growth and credit-sensitive sectors:
  - Widespread reports across districts of increased usage of revolving credit lines, suggesting households and firms are leaning more on credit—supporting near-term spend but raising vulnerability.
  - Broad weakening in residential loan demand across districts, pointing to a faster cooling in housing.
  - Price pressures remain broad-based (construction inputs, food, energy, commodities), reinforcing the Fed’s focus on inflation.
Implications: Tighter bank lending supply plus greater reliance on revolving credit and weaker housing demand amplify headwinds beyond the macro statement alone. Inflation breadth limits near-term policy relief. Net tone shifts more negative than the SLOOS-only read.
